prefers: Continue governing arrangements with ACT and NZ First if numbers allow (2023 coalition partners).
rulesOut: Ruled out Opportunity (tax/spend criteria confirmed by PMO).
Ruled out a National-Labour grand coalition.
Campaign framing excludes Labour, Greens, and Te Pati Maori as governing partners.
bottomLines: No new taxes to be solidified in any renewed coalition agreement (2026 campaign).
Partner test: will not do business with parties that want to spend more, tax more, borrow more.
national.summary: National anchors the centre-right bloc with ACT and NZ First, has ruled out Opportunity and a grand coalition with Labour, and campaigns for a strong National party vote while publishing no-new-taxes as a coalition condition.

prefers: Continued working relationship with the Greens; door open to Opportunity.
Could work with Te Pati Maori; senior government roles for TPM described as unlikely.
Minority government with confidence-and-supply (rather than full coalition) left on the table.
rulesOut: Will not work with parties in the current government (National, ACT, NZ First).
Official 2026 rule-out of NZ First (reported unanimous caucus).
Will not form a government with ACT.
bottomLines: Will not agree to abolish prisons or a Treaty Ombudsman with veto over Parliament (stated incompatibilities with some Te Pati Maori proposals).
Will not adopt Green wealth/corporate tax packages that contradict Labour's campaign tax commitments.
labour.summary: Labour has hardened rule-outs against the incumbent bloc (especially NZ First and ACT), keeps Greens and Opportunity in play, leaves a narrower path with Te Pati Maori, and prefers not to adopt partners major tax packages beyond its own campaign commitments.

prefers: Positions for a change of government with Labour; historically provided confidence and supply / cooperation.
rulesOut: Opposes continuing the National-ACT-NZ First government agenda (campaign opposition posture).
bottomLines: Major tax and redistribution proposals (e.g. wealth tax framing) remain core platform asks in negotiations with Labour, though Labour has refused to adopt them.
green.summary: The Greens seek to replace the current government alongside Labour and push progressive tax and climate priorities; published 2026 materials emphasise policy ambition more than a fixed multi-party rule-out list.

prefers: Governing partnership with National (and NZ First as in 2023 National-ACT agreement).
rulesOut: Campaign framing against Labour/Greens/Te Pati Maori forming government.
bottomLines: 2023 National-ACT agreement items remain a reference for ACT priorities (e.g. Treaty Principles process to select committee, regulatory reform).
act.summary: ACT positions as National's classical-liberal governing partner and campaigns to keep Labour, Greens and Te Pati Maori out of government, with 2023 coalition text documenting prior red-line bargains.

prefers: Governing arrangements with National (2023 National-NZ First coalition).
rulesOut: Ruled out doing a deal with Labour for 2026 (repeated public statements).
bottomLines: 2023 agreement priorities (e.g. foreign buyers tax blocked; smokefree repeal; Fees Free switch) show NZ First uses coalition deals to hard-wire vetoes.
nz-first.summary: NZ First campaigns as a populist partner able to restrain or reshape National-led governments; 2023 coalition text is the clearest published record of its deal-breaker style, while 2026 rule-outs focus on blocking Labour.

prefers: Change-of-government path with Labour/Greens; campaign messaging has urged party votes for Labour or Greens while focusing on Maori electorates.
rulesOut: Opposes the current governing coalition's Treaty and Maori policy agenda.
bottomLines: Te Tiriti entrenchment / constitutional pathway: independent Te Tiriti commission powers, binding Waitangi Tribunal recommendations, and related funding proposals (Labour has rejected key elements).
te-pati-maori.summary: Te Pati Maori runs an electorate-centred strategy with a one-person list and has published Te Tiriti constitutional demands as negotiation bottom lines; it seeks a left-leaning change of government while Labour has left the door ajar but rejected some TPM proposals.

prefers: Open to coalition or confidence-and-supply with either National or Labour.
rulesOut: National has ruled Opportunity out (external constraint); Opportunity still says its door to National remains open.
bottomLines: Empower Commerce Commission on anti-competitive market power (including structural separation tools).
10-year cross-party health plan with funding/workforce/infrastructure commitments.
Phase out bottom trawling (start with damaged inshore areas).
Recommit to Paris obligations and protect Climate Change Commission independence.
Will not support a government with Winston Peters as Foreign Minister (reported 2026 statement).
opportunity.summary: Opportunity published five formal 2026 bottom lines and says it will talk to either major party; National has ruled Opportunity out over tax policy while Opportunity says its door remains open.

alliance.summary: Alliance contests the 2026 party vote with left/democratic-socialist policy; a clear published coalition preference matrix was not found in sources checked.

animal-justice.summary: Animal Justice focuses on animal-rights policy; no clear multi-party coalition rule-in/rule-out statement found in sources checked.

prefers: Would steer supporters toward a major party that commits to adult cannabis legalisation (conditional preference).
alcp.summary: ALCP is organised around cannabis law reform and has said it would encourage supporters to back a major party that commits to adult legalisation; it has no published multi-party coalition matrix beyond that issue.

conservative.summary: Conservative Party NZ contests on socially conservative themes; a detailed 2026 coalition preference list was not found in sources checked.

free-palestine.summary: Free Palestine campaigns on Palestine-related foreign policy; formal coalition preference statements were not found in sources checked.

nz-loyal.summary: NZ Loyal contests with loyalty/sovereignty messaging; clear governing-partner preferences were not found in sources checked.

outdoors-freedom.summary: NZ Outdoors & Freedom emphasises civil liberties and direct democracy; published coalition red-lines were not found in sources checked.

prefers: Open to post-election talks with parties across the spectrum (including National) if that serves Te Tai Tokerau.
te-tai-tokerau.summary: Regional party focused on the Te Tai Tokerau electorate; leader messaging has left room for talks with National and others if that advances the rohe, without a published national bottom-lines list.

vision.summary: Vision New Zealand contests the party vote; a clear published coalition preference matrix was not found in sources checked.

womens-rights.summary: Women's Rights Party focuses on sex-based rights policy; formal coalition rule-ins/outs were not found in sources checked.
